atoms.text: To measure things precisely we use units. Units are defined lengths, so that everybody measures in the same way. But which units are there? How do we use them?

atoms.b: ((++Metres --Kilos)) and ((++centimetres --degrees)) are both used to measure length. They are both part of the metric system.
The shortened form of metres is ((++m l)) and the shortened form of centimetres is ((++cm kg)).

hint.text: Look closely. The shortened forms are very similar to the words they represent.

instruction.text: Match the units to their shortened forms.

atoms.b: One metre is as long as ((--10 ++100 --1000)) centimetres.
One centimetre is much ((++smaller larger)) than one metre.

instruction.text: Look at the measurements and select the object with the same height as the board below.

hint.text: One metre is as long as 100 centimetres.

trainers.finishSound: Correct! One metre is the same length 100 centimetres.

instruction.text: Look at the measurements and select the object with the same height as the lamp below.

hint.text: 1 metre is as long as 100 centimetres.

trainers.finishSound: Well done! 100 centimetres is the same length as one metre.
